narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 69.9% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class ranking at the end of your third year was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Being in the bottom decile (1 out of 10) is substantially lower than the average ranking of about 5.8 among students who were accepted. Your first-year ranking in the second decile also contributed to the negative outlook, though less dramatically; again this sits far below the typical sixth-decile performance of admitted students.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.0 worked in the opposite direction. It provided a modest positive signal toward passing the bar, but this encouraging effect was not large enough to offset the impact of your class rankings.

Taken together, the model saw your relatively low standing within your law school cohorts as the dominant reason to expect difficulty passing the bar, which led directly to the rejection.

What you should do next is focus on improving your class rank in the remaining years and consider targeted bar-preparation resources that have helped students in similar positions. Strengthening your academic performance now can meaningfully change future predictions and open doors to admission or reconsideration. (248 words)
